A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DP-FUSION research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison across rearrangement and renumbering.

before.justification: V2 reports original document-privatization, token-recovery, tagging and prompt-injection experiments on TAB-ECHR, MACCROBAT and HotpotQA.

after.justification: V4 retains these empirical results and adds downstream question-answering evaluations, base-model comparisons and a Rényi-order ablation in Appendices A.23–A.26.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, line 3 changes the shared continuation context from D union D_out to D_out, removing the full private document from the public branch's input. This localized pseudocode correction aligns the algorithm with the intended public/private separation already described in v2; distribution mixing, bisection and the single-group variant remain.

E1.justification: The original TAB-ECHR, MACCROBAT and HotpotQA coverage is retained. V4 adds factual multiple-choice question answering on ECHR chunks, evaluated both after document privatization and with DPI applied during answer generation (A.23–A.24). These introduce substantive downstream tasks and deployment scenarios beyond the earlier evaluations.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged in the retained privatization, tagging and injection experiments. The new downstream tables use the existing DP-Decoding, DP-Prompt and No-DPI baselines. Mistral and Llama are additional base-model configurations for evaluating DP-FUSION.

E3.justification: The added downstream protocol uses 100 chunks of 200 Qwen-tokenizer tokens, GPT-4o-generated questions and distractors, four-option answer extraction and accuracy scoring, with separate document-privatization and output-generation procedures. A.25–A.26 add Mistral-7B/Llama-3-8B configurations and an α sweep from 1.5 to 3.0 at fixed β=0.01. The original main experimental settings are retained.

E4.justification: A.25 newly examines dependence on the base-model family across five divergence settings, while A.26 tests sensitivity to Rényi order against the α=2 reference. These extend robustness and parameter validation. Candidate-set, tagger, single-group, medical-dataset, injection and mixing-parameter analyses were already present in v2.

E5.justification: Both versions report Wilson-score intervals in Figures 11–12, 95% confidence intervals in Figure 14 and unspecified multiple runs in the privacy-accounting analysis. V4 introduces no new run counts, seeds or performance-uncertainty procedures. Table 14's standard deviations describe chunk characteristics rather than uncertainty in experimental performance.

E6.justification: Table 1 and most earlier appendix results are retained. New Tables 16–19 report downstream accuracy, model-relative win rates and α sensitivity; for example, DP-FUSION at αβ=0.01 reports 37% accuracy after privatization and 52% during live generation, under distinct settings. Table 10 adds single-group result details and drops most Sim-Priv entries. Table 17 reverses the reused NER/original-document LOSS values, creating a reporting inconsistency.

T1.justification: The adjacency definition, privacy assumptions, composition bound and monotonicity proof remain substantively unchanged. V4's new numbered Definition 5 restates the symmetric Rényi divergence already defined in v2 Section 4 and used in Algorithm 1; it does not introduce a new mathematical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: token-level private inference, improved privacy–utility trade-offs, approximately sixfold lower perplexity than DPI baselines, and prompt-injection mitigation. The additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: Section 5.4 newly attributes the small ASR advantage over NER to randomness from distribution mixing. Section 4.1 adds a near-single-forward-pass latency claim under parallelization, and A.25 discusses Qwen's advantage while acknowledging that its cause remains unresolved. Existing tagging, computational-cost and sensitive-token-density limitations are largely retained.

D1.justification: V4 adds a reproducibility statement and links to the project's GitHub repository, PyPI package and deployed application, absent from v2. It newly specifies δ=0.001 and equal-length underscore padding, clarifies baseline prompting, and supplies downstream question-generation/evaluation templates, chunk statistics and additional model identifiers. These substantially expand documented implementation and access information.

R1.justification: Section 4 expands the positioning relative to PATE, SUBMIX and PMixED, including SUBMIX's budget-exhaustion limitation and PMixED's closed-form RDP accounting. The Dwork and Feldman (2018) private-prediction citation and reference are removed. The broader literature coverage remains stable.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose are retained. V4 makes localized rewrites and explanatory additions, especially in Sections 4–6, adds ethics/reproducibility and LLM-writing disclosures, and renumbers the existing appendix sections before adding A.23–A.26. This is a limited narrative revision.

P2.justification: V4 adopts ICLR title, heading and running-header formatting and extensively reflows figures and tables. Figure 13 is redrawn with a full 0–1 privacy axis and changed styling; Table 10 changes columns and grouping; Tables 14–19 are added. Existing Figures 11–12 are relocated, while the original diagrams and paraphrase examples are retained.

improvement.justification: V4 offers a limited net improvement through the Algorithm 1 correction, clearer implementation/access information and additional downstream, model and α evaluations. These gains are weakened by the new live-chat section: Table 17 reuses privacy scores from another setting, reverses the NER/original-document LOSS entries, and its discussion quotes accuracies inconsistent with the table. Consequently, the expanded evidence improves coverage but does not provide consistently stronger validation.
